Why this split
Search

Assumption: Leaning on public B2B benchmarks, the best available without accessiBe’s own data. Real numbers would shift this based on better understanding of channel-level conversions, funnel-performance.
Ranked 1 of 3 by expected impact
Bet 1: Adjust the offer
Lead with an expert audit, and explain why accessiBe before asking for a meeting.
Why?
Current CTAs push for a demo/meeting
The scan results and report email ask for a demo, with little on the why and how of AccessiBe.
The scan draws tool seekers
Many ad keywords are “website checker” searches, not buying searches. Good for volume, question quality
Upmarket rivals sell audits
Level Access’s ads lead with a demo, an expert-led audit and more specific in-depth reports.
The test
What: Value-added results page and email vs. today’s, then an audit offer.
Read in: 2 to 3 weeks (page), 4 to 6 weeks (ads)
Scale if: Cost per MQL falls 25% or more
Stop if: Demo requests drop 20% with no MQL gain
What it takes
Page copy, some developer support, some new ad creative and possible sales enablement support. No added media spend. Would be roughly 4 weeks to launch. 
How I’d know I was wrong
The audit offer doesn’t beat the free scan on MQL rate.
Ranked 2 of 3 by expected impact
Bet 2: Target named accounts
Scan about 1,000 mid-market sites and offer no-strings personal risk snapshots.
Why it should work
Specific beats generic
Top targets receive a snapshot of their own results, gives a reason to talk.
Pain point messaging: Lawsuits are rising and they are at risk
Federal website accessibility suits rose 27% in 2025, to 3,117.
LinkedIn and Email testing
Target company lists to see if offer resonates
The test
What: Top 200 accounts by severity get snapshot creative, the rest get standard.
Read in: 6 weeks (demo rate), 90 days (pipeline)
Scale if: Demo rate beats standard
Stop if: Cost per demo runs 2x higher
What it takes
An account list, scan access for about 1,000 sites (where can AI support?), snapshot email creative and an sales support to rank accounts. 
How I’d know I was wrong
Personalized messaging and scans don’t lift demo rate, or too few mid-market accounts turn up.
Before scaling 
Does pilot outperform the generic test.
Ranked 3 of 3 by expected impact
Bet 3: 'Human' follow-up on top scans
Put a person behind the best scans, then follow up with past scanners using fresh results.
Why it should work
A big pool to mine
accessScan reports 650,000+ scans a year, and past scanners can be re-scanned.
The report doesn’t say why accessiBe
It says what’s wrong, not who should fix it or how. Appendix A
Deliverability is a risk
My test report email landed in spam, risk of sending email from a generic “support” sender. Test sending from real rep address or at least less generic email. Appendix B
The test
What: Top-tier scans get a personal rep email vs. automated email only. Past scanners get a fresh scan, with a no-contact holdout.
Read in: 4 weeks (replies, meetings, MQLs)
Scale if: Meeting rate is about 2x control
Stop if: Replies are low, or rep meeting to qualification is unimproved
What it takes
CRM automation audit. Build workflows to score leads and assign rep to send automated emails. About 2 weeks to launch.
How I’d know I was wrong
Replies and meetings don’t beat the automated email.
Guardrails
Pilot in the US only. Exclude all current customers and open deals.

Growing upmarket:  SMB to Mid-Market
Equip the champion and reach the whole buying group.

Every channel points to one thing: the account’s own accessScan result.
Who

200 to 2,000 employees, web-facing

The rest run automated

Scan snapshot
Their own result, in plain English
Role one-pagers
Legal, developer, executive

Exposure and what to do
Sample audit
Free, engaged accounts only
Assumption: We have support and collaborative working relationship with Sales leadership and team Open question: is it acceptable to scan accounts that never asked? My default is yes: public pages only, wording reviewed by legal, “exposure” not “non-compliant”, and an easy opt-out. I’d test it against scanning only after someone engages. Pivot: If this is out-of-bounds, we market the scan itself, but with some personalization

From the SMB playbook: keep, change, stop
Going upmarket adds a new motion. It doesn't replace the one that works.
Keep
Search capture
Buyers searching today still convert.
accessScan at the top
It remains the front door.
A self-serve lane
Small buyers still buy without a call.
Change
The goal
From leads to engaged accounts and pipeline.
The follow-up
A person behind the best scans.
The handoff
Sales sees which roles engaged and what they read.
Stop
Optimizing for cheap form fills
Cost per lead hid weak quality.
Treating every lead the same
A mid-market buying group isn't a self-serve signup.
With Sales
Agree what a qualified account is in week 1.
With RevOps
Track accounts and roles, not just leads. Create necessary scoring and measurement as needed
With leadership
Communicate strategy. Share dates for the leading signals. Clear reporting of results.

Assumptions: 
  • The sheet is several months of Meta lead-gen, so I show shares, not monthly dollars. 
  • An MQL is a fair stand-in for quality. With 41 MQLs in all, the performance is not driving the results expected
  • There are other campaigns running on META - including remarketing which I have been served up in high-frequency. The recommendations here are only for Lead Gen data provided. 
What this data can't tell us
It counts leads and MQLs. It doesn't show what happened after, or who they were.
The gap
What I'd need
Whether MQLs become pipeline (SQL)
Sales accepted, opportunities and closed-won by ad group, with deal size.
Who the leads are
Company size, role and segment from the CRM, to judge fit with mid-market targets.
What Meta actually influenced
Is Meta a lead source or an assist? The attribution method (clicks or views) and a holdout test. Meta reports 2,465 leads, the CRM shows 356.
What is a profitable cost per MQL?
Conversion rates by stage, average closed-won revenue and, even better, customer lifetime value (LTV).
How remarketing performs
Spend, conversions and audiences for re-marketing campaigns. 
Fit with upmarket goals?
Pipeline per dollar from mid-market accounts, not leads or MQLs.
Assumptions: 
  • This is lead-gen camapaign aimed at a smaller buyer. Until we see pipeline by segment, treat these results as a guide to quality, not proof of what works upmarket.
Summary: Focus on qualified accounts, not just leads
